_doc: Data-driven audit of the cloud-cgc-pub-mcp GraphRAG stack. This file is the SOURCE OF TRUTH; docs/graphrag-architecture.md is a human view of it. Each invariant carries a re-runnable `probe` (tool + args) so the audit is a regression gate, not a one-off. To refresh: run every probe, write the result into `observed`, set `status` (PASS = claim holds, FAIL = violated, OPEN = not yet validated), and fix anything that regressed from PASS. Continuous-improvement loop: an invariant is DONE when status=PASS and its `fix` is empty.
generator: manual adversarial probe session (claude-opus-4-8); automate via a workflow that iterates `invariants[].probe`

codegraph.store: in-memory graph, rebuilt per query with a 5-min TTL cache
codegraph.note: The ONLY subsystem that has symbol/defines/code_depends_on. They are synthesized from code-signatures at load time and exist nowhere else.

kgstore.source: separate ingest pipeline: octocode per-repo mirror (file + sibling_module + parent_module) + infra topology delta
kgstore.note: Does NOT contain symbol/defines/code_depends_on. `imports` exists as a table but is empty; imports live as an array field on `file`.

octocode.store: LanceDB vectors + LLM GraphRAG, per-repo indices
octocode.source: per-repo semantic index (reindexed independently per repo)
octocode.note: Uses NEW repo names (cloud-infra/cloud-unix). Its own SurrealDB mirror uses OLD names (cloud/unix). Reindex freshness is per-repo and uneven.

divergence_matrix._doc: What each element counts in CodeGraph `overview` vs what is actually queryable in the SurrealDB kg-store. The overview banner sums ONLY CodeGraph; it does not describe kgstore.
rows: 0 — table exists but empty; imports = field on `file`
same 6, but only 3 have a repo node

invariants.title: overview counts must be queryable somewhere
invariants.claim: Every node/edge table `cgc_codegraph_overview` reports is reachable by at least one query tool.

probe.surql: SELECT count() FROM symbol GROUP ALL
SELECT count() FROM defines GROUP ALL
SELECT count() FROM code_depends_on GROUP ALL

invariants.expected: counts > 0 in kgstore for symbol/defines/code_depends_on, OR overview labels them codegraph-only
invariants.observed: overview: symbol=29660, defines=32510, code_depends_on=3959; kgstore: 0/0/0 (tables absent). ~65k claimed elements unreachable via SurrealQL.
invariants.root_cause: codegraph.ts synthesizes symbol/defines/code_depends_on in-memory from code-signatures; they are never ingested into SurrealDB. overview reports the in-memory graph only.

fix.change: Label overview rows by which tool can query them (codegraph-only vs kgstore-backed), OR ingest symbol/defines into SurrealDB. Cheapest: annotate overview output with `queryable_via`.

invariants.title: single repo vocabulary across subsystems
invariants.claim: A repo has ONE identifier used by codegraph, kgstore, and octocode.

probe.surql: SELECT array::group(repo) AS repos FROM file GROUP ALL

probe.note: compare against octocode.repo_enum in this file

invariants.expected: identical repo id set across all three
invariants.observed: file.repo & code-signatures: cloud/unix/front/tools/cloud-data/front-data. repo table: cloud, cloud_data (id underscore, name hyphen), unix. octocode enum: cloud-infra/cloud-unix/front/cloud-data/front-data/cloud-android/cloud-data-my-ai-memory. THREE vocabularies.
invariants.root_cause: code-signatures filenames, the delta repo-node builder, and octocode's index registry were named at different times across the repo rename (cloud->cloud-infra, unix->cloud-unix).

fix.change: Adopt the new canonical names everywhere; add an alias map at the ingest boundary so old snapshots still resolve.

invariants.title: no dangling file->repo
invariants.claim: Every value of file.repo has a corresponding node in the `repo` table.

probe.surql: SELECT array::group(repo) AS repos FROM file GROUP ALL

invariants.expected: 6 repo nodes matching the 6 file.repo values
invariants.observed: files reference 6 repos; only 3 repo nodes exist (cloud, cloud_data, unix). front / front-data / tools (1135 files) have NO repo node.
invariants.root_cause: delta builder only emits repo nodes for the 3 infra-tracked repos; code-signatures for front/tools/front-data add files but no repo node.

fix.change: Emit a repo node for every distinct repo seen in code-signatures; reconcile id (cloud_data) vs name (cloud-data) to one form.

invariants.title: belongs_to_repo attributes modules to their real repo
invariants.claim: module -> belongs_to_repo -> repo points to the repo the module actually lives in.

probe.surql: SELECT out AS repo_node, count() AS n FROM belongs_to_repo GROUP BY repo_node

invariants.observed: all 62 belongs_to_repo edges point to repo:cloud. repo:unix and repo:cloud_data have zero incoming.
invariants.root_cause: all modeled modules are infra modules (they DO live in cloud-infra), but the edge then carries no cross-repo signal — attribution is degenerate, not wrong-but-useful.

fix.change: Only meaningful once code modules from unix/front are modeled; until then document belongs_to_repo as infra-only.

invariants.title: tool documentation examples execute and return rows
invariants.claim: Every example query in a tool's own description runs and returns data.

probe.surql: SELECT count() AS n FROM file WHERE repo = 'cloud-infra' GROUP ALL

probe.note: cgc_kgstore_query description ships: "...WHERE repo='cloud-infra'..." and "...WHERE repo='cloud-unix'..."

invariants.observed: empty result — real vocab is repo='cloud' / 'unix', so both documented examples return zero rows.
invariants.root_cause: tool description written against the new repo names; the ingested data uses the old names (see INV-02).

fix.change: Fix the example strings to the vocab actually ingested, OR fix the vocab (INV-02) so the examples become true.

invariants.title: kgstore.overview reflects real tables
invariants.claim: cgc_kgstore_overview lists exactly the tables INFO FOR DB reports.

probe.note: compare against NODE_TABLES/EDGE_TABLES hardcoded in kgstore.ts

invariants.expected: hardcoded lists == INFO FOR DB tables
invariants.observed: kgstore.ts hardcodes phantom `documentation`, `log`, `connected_to` (absent from DB) and omits real `parent_module` + `imports`.
invariants.root_cause: NODE_TABLES/EDGE_TABLES are a hand-maintained constant that drifted from the schema.

fix.change: Derive the table list from INFO FOR DB at runtime instead of hardcoding it.

invariants.title: file inventory agrees between CodeGraph and kg-store
invariants.claim: CodeGraph and SurrealDB scan the same file set.

probe.surql: SELECT repo, count() AS n FROM file GROUP BY repo

invariants.observed: overview total=2905 (cloud 1435, unix 387, front 915, tools 63, cloud-data 106, front-data 1). kgstore total=3843 (cloud 2148, unix 347, front 938, tools 190, cloud-data 213, front-data 7).
invariants.root_cause: CodeGraph reads image-baked code-signatures (frozen at build); SurrealDB reads octocode's live mirror. Different scanners, different include rules, different times.

fix.change: Share one file-enumeration (same ignore rules); or rebuild code-signatures on every image build and pin both to the same commit.

invariants.title: infra edge counts agree between delta and kg-store
invariants.claim: routes_to (and peers) count the same in overview and SurrealDB.

probe.surql: SELECT count() FROM routes_to GROUP ALL

invariants.root_cause: infra delta baked into the image is one generation behind the SurrealDB ingest.

fix.change: Rebuild build-kg-graph_delta.json in the same job that ingests SurrealDB.

invariants.title: code_depends_on name matches its semantics

probe.surql: SELECT out.name AS target, count() AS fanin FROM code_depends_on GROUP BY target ORDER BY fanin DESC LIMIT 5

probe.note: codegraph.ts comment: local import => `imports` (file->file); external import => `code_depends_on` (file->package)

invariants.observed: code_depends_on targets are `package:` nodes (external deps). File->file lives under `imports`. The name overpromises; fan-in aggregation on it is meaningless. (Also unreachable via kgstore, see INV-01.)

fix.change: Rename to depends_on_package, or fold into a typed `depends_on` with a kind field; document that file->file = imports.

invariants.title: querying a missing table is an error, not silent zero
invariants.claim: A query against a non-existent table surfaces the mistake.

probe.surql: SELECT count() FROM this_table_does_not_exist GROUP ALL

invariants.expected: an error or explicit 'unknown table' signal
invariants.observed: returns count:0 (SurrealDB returns empty for missing tables). Bad SYNTAX errors (400) but a missing TABLE silently zeros — indistinguishable from a truly empty table. Masks INV-01 for callers.
invariants.root_cause: SurrealDB semantics; the tool does not pre-validate the table against INFO FOR DB.

fix.change: Before executing, extract FROM targets and warn if any is not in INFO FOR DB.

invariants.title: octocode indices are uniformly fresh
invariants.claim: All repos' octocode indices reflect the latest commit.
invariants.observed: cloud-infra index FRESH (shows cloud-cgc-pub-mcp v7.0.0, new .mcp.json names). cloud-unix index STALE (still shows cloud-cgc-mcp / diego-personal-data / unix from before the 2026-08-27 rename).
invariants.root_cause: reindex is triggered per-repo and did not run for cloud-unix after the rename push.

fix.change: Trigger octocode reindex on push for every indexed repo; expose last-indexed commit per repo via cgc_octocode_index.

invariants.title: service version is single-sourced
invariants.claim: The cgc service reports one version.
invariants.root_cause: version hand-edited in code, not read from package.json.

invariants.title: octocode graphrag operations return bounded output
invariants.claim: cgc_octocode_graphrag search/get-node/get-relationships/find-path return a summary, not the raw graph.
invariants.observed: operation=search dumped a ~4MB blob (186k lines) to a tool-results file. get-node/get-relationships/find-path NOT YET validated (need node ids).
invariants.root_cause: unknown — needs investigation; possibly returns all matched nodes with full content.

fix.change: Cap result size / add top-k; then validate get-relationships and find-path and move this to PASS or a concrete FAIL.

passing_controls.title: kgstore read-only guard
passing_controls.detail: UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE/DEFINE refused by kgstore.ts MUTATING guard. Load-bearing: SurrealDB tables are PERMISSIONS NONE (wide open), so this app-layer guard is the only write protection. Keep it covered by a test.

passing_controls.title: cross-layer impact_analysis
passing_controls.detail: impact_analysis(c3-infra-mcp) correctly returns domain + module dependents across the infra/code boundary.

passing_controls.title: directed trace honesty
passing_controls.detail: trace_call_path returns 'no path (directed)' with a swap hint instead of a false path.

passing_controls.title: routes_to catalog correct
passing_controls.detail: routes_to.in.fqdn -> out.name matches the live MCP hub (mcp.diegonmarcos.com/c3-infra-mcp -> c3-infra-mcp, etc).

probe.surql: SELECT in.fqdn AS domain, out.name AS service FROM routes_to WHERE out.name = 'c3-infra-mcp'

frameworks._doc: Researched external standards (2026) to raise this stack from ad-hoc to industry-grade. Each maps to invariants above and to the deeper_tests below. Sources in graphrag-architecture.md section 6.

adopt.name: PG-Schema / PG-Keys
adopt.what: Declarative schema + key/participation/referential-integrity constraints for Labeled Property Graphs; basis of the GQL (ISO 39075:2024) and SQL/PGQ standards.
adopt.why_here: kg-store IS an LPG (SurrealDB). A PG-Schema gives node/edge types, mandatory participation, and referential integrity as DATA, not code. Directly closes INV-03 (dangling file->repo) and INV-04 (belongs_to_repo participation).
adopt.action: Author a pg-schema.json (node types, edge endpoints, keys, participation) and generate the deeper_tests.schema_constraints SurrealQL from it.

adopt.name: SHACL family (Trav-SHACL, xpSHACL)
adopt.what: Shapes-Constraint-Language pattern: declare shapes, validator emits a violation report; xpSHACL adds human-readable explanations.
adopt.why_here: SurrealDB is not RDF, so we borrow the PATTERN, not the tech: shapes -> a violations report with an explanation per failure. schema_constraints below is our SHACL-report equivalent.
adopt.action: Every constraint returns violating rows (not a bool) + an `explain` string, mirroring xpSHACL.

adopt.name: RAGAS
adopt.what: RAG-eval metrics: context precision, context recall, faithfulness, answer relevancy; plus retrieval MRR. LLM-as-judge.
adopt.why_here: octocode/graphrag retrieval is currently UNTESTED for quality (INV-13 only checks output size). RAGAS gives measurable retrieval quality.
adopt.action: See deeper_tests.retrieval_quality — a golden Q->expected-nodes set scored on context precision/recall + MRR.

adopt.name: GraphRAG-Bench
adopt.what: GraphRAG benchmark with 4 task levels (fact retrieval -> complex/multi-hop reasoning -> summarization -> novel generation); metrics Accuracy, ROUGE-L, coverage.
adopt.why_here: Structures our golden set by reasoning depth so we test multi-hop graph traversal (this stack's whole point), not just fact lookup.
adopt.action: Tag each golden question with a level 1-4; require >=1 multi-hop (level 2) case per infra<->code boundary.

adopt.name: SCIP (+ Kythe/Glean)
adopt.what: SCIP = Sourcegraph Code Intelligence Protocol: protobuf index of documents -> symbols -> occurrences -> relationships, with cross-repo monikers; successor to LSIF. Kythe/Glean are the Google/Meta equivalents.
adopt.why_here: The home-grown code-signatures derive is the root of INV-07 (2905 vs 3843 file scans diverge) and the weak symbol layer. A standard indexer yields ONE deterministic file+symbol set both stores can share, with real definition/reference xrefs.
adopt.action: Evaluate emitting SCIP per repo (scip-typescript, scip-python, rust-analyzer SCIP) and ingesting THAT into both CodeGraph and kg-store, replacing bespoke code-signatures.

deeper_tests._doc: Executable test suites beyond the divergence invariants. schema_constraints run NOW against SurrealDB (seeded with real observed violations 2026-08-27). cross_store_consistency compares CodeGraph vs kg-store. retrieval_quality is the RAGAS/GraphRAG-Bench harness to build.

schema_constraints._doc: PG-Keys/SHACL-style. Each rule's SurrealQL returns VIOLATING rows; expected = empty. Seeded with observed results.

rules.rule: every file.repo has a repo node
rules.surql: SELECT repo, count() AS n FROM file WHERE repo NOT IN (SELECT VALUE name FROM repo) GROUP BY repo
rules.explain: repo nodes only emitted for cloud/cloud_data/unix; see INV-03

rules.rule: every routes_to edge resolves to a named service
rules.surql: SELECT count() AS v FROM routes_to WHERE out.name = NONE GROUP ALL
SELECT VALUE c FROM (SELECT name, count() AS c FROM service GROUP BY name) WHERE c > 1
SELECT count() AS v FROM file WHERE repo = NONE OR repo = '' GROUP ALL

rules.rule: repo node id-slug equals its name (no underscore/hyphen drift)
rules.observed: repo:cloud_data has name 'cloud-data' (underscore id vs hyphen name)
rules.explain: id/name normalization drift; breaks any join that reconstructs repo:<name>

rules.rule: every repo node has >=1 incoming belongs_to_repo
rules.surql: SELECT out AS repo, count() AS n FROM belongs_to_repo GROUP BY repo
rules.observed: only repo:cloud (n=62); repo:unix and repo:cloud_data have zero

cross_store_consistency._doc: Assert CodeGraph `overview` and SurrealDB agree where they model the same thing. codegraph values via cgc_codegraph_overview; kgstore via the surql shown.

checks.kgstore_surql: SELECT count() FROM file GROUP ALL
SELECT count() FROM routes_to GROUP ALL
SELECT count() FROM symbol GROUP ALL
SELECT count() FROM service GROUP ALL
checks.observed: both report 60 services — verify names match, not just counts

retrieval_quality._doc: RAGAS + GraphRAG-Bench harness for octocode/graphrag. NOT YET BUILT. Build a golden set, then score. This is the biggest blind spot: search/graphrag correctness is currently unmeasured.
requirements: >= 20 questions, >= 5 at level 2 (multi-hop across the infra<->code boundary)
each infra<->code trace (e.g. domain -> service -> module -> repo) has a level-2 case
score context_precision/recall on expected_nodes; MRR on rank of first expected node
seed level-1 cases from the passing FUNC-01/02/03 controls above

example_golden.question: Which service does mcp.diegonmarcos.com/c3-infra-mcp route to?

args.surql: SELECT out.name FROM routes_to WHERE in.fqdn = 'mcp.diegonmarcos.com/c3-infra-mcp'

example_golden.question: If c3-infra-mcp changes, which domain and which module are impacted?
